page: Microsoft Azure D16pls_v6 is an ARM-based compute instance powered by Microsoft's custom ARM Neoverse-N2 architecture. Running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor, this virtual machine provisions 16 dedicated physical cores and 16 vCPUs operating at a clock speed of 3.4 GHz with 1 thread per core. The processor is configured with 64 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and a large 128 MB L3 cache pool. It incorporates 32.0 GB of system memory, providing a lean ratio of 2.0 GB of RAM per vCPU without any bundled local storage or integrated GPU hardware.

Benchmark evaluations indicate consistent computational throughput and notable memory subsystem performance. The instance achieved a top-tier PassMark memory score of 3233.3 and registered strong uncached memory bandwidth, delivering 310.02 GB/sec in 256 MB block reads and 124.68 GB/sec in block writes. Single-threaded gzip compression reached a strong 33.11 GB/sec. General compute benchmarks, including Geekbench multi-core (14659.0), stress-ng multi-core (33153.41), and PassMark CPU (14712.64), consistently place in the middle 50% tier, showing steady execution across all 16 physical cores.

The 1:2 memory-to-vCPU ratio represents an intentional architectural tradeoff that favors compute density over large in-memory capacities. While small 135M model LLM prompt processing delivers an average 678.45 tokens per second, larger 7B model prompt processing drops to 24.69 tokens per second, reflecting the constraints of CPU-bound inference and a smaller memory footprint. The omission of bundled local storage requires attached remote storage for persistent data access.

Given its high core allocation and fast memory subsystem, the Microsoft Azure D16pls_v6 is suitable for CPU-bound microservices, web serving clusters, containerized compilation tasks, batch data transformation, and distributed worker nodes that do not require extensive per-core RAM.
